title: Tez nutq va turli aksentlarni tushunish
goal_uz: Dars oxirida tez nutqdagi kuchsiz shakllar, bog‘lanish, elizia va assimilyatsiyani taniysiz, kamida beshta asosiy aksentni belgilari bo‘yicha farqlaysiz va eshitilmagan so‘zni kontekstdan tiklaysiz yoki xushmuomala aniqlashtirasiz.

scenes.title: Tez nutqni ochamiz
board: Lesson: Fast speech and accents
(Tez nutq va turli aksentlarni tushunish)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda murakkab matnda muallifning maqsadi va munosabatini aniqlashni o‘rgandik: hedge, pozitsiya belgilari, fakt va fikr. Bugun yozuvdan quloqqa o‘tamiz. Dars oxirida tabiiy tez nutqdagi qisqarishlarni taniysiz, asosiy aksentlarni farqlaysiz va bir so‘zni eshitmay qolsangiz ham, gapning mazmunini yo‘qotmaysiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time we read between the lines. Today we listen between the words, because real speakers don't talk like textbooks.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. O‘tgan safar satrlar orasini o‘qidik. Bugun so‘zlar orasini tinglaymiz, chunki haqiqiy so‘zlovchilar darslikdagidek gapirmaydi.

scenes.title: Nega tez nutq qiyin?
board: Written: What do you want to do?
Spoken: Whaddaya wanna do?
Same words, different sound shape
scenes.say_native: Avval muammoni tushunaylik. Siz so‘zlarni yozma shaklda yaxshi bilasiz, lekin tez nutqda ular boshqacha eshitiladi. “What do you want to do?” degan gap og‘zaki nutqda taxminan “Whaddaya wanna do?” bo‘lib ketadi. So‘zlar yo‘qolmaydi, ular qisqaradi, birlashadi va o‘zgaradi. Bu tasodif emas, tizim. Tizimni bilsangiz, quloq tez o‘rganadi.
scenes.say: What do you want to do? In fast speech: Whaddaya wanna do? Nothing is missing. The words have simply changed shape.
scenes.say_uz: Nima qilmoqchisan? Tez nutqda: Whaddaya wanna do? Hech narsa yo‘qolmagan. So‘zlar shunchaki shaklini o‘zgartirgan.

scenes.title: Urg‘u ritmi va kuchsiz shakllar
board: English is stress-timed
Stressed: content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives)
Unstressed: function words → weak forms /ə/

examples.t: I want to GO to the SHOPS.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi nuqta: bog‘langan nutq. Ingliz tili urg‘u ritmiga ega: urg‘uli bo‘g‘inlar taxminan teng oraliqda keladi, ular orasidagi urg‘usiz so‘zlar esa siqiladi. Mazmunli so‘zlar, ya’ni ot, fe’l, sifat urg‘u oladi. Yordamchi so‘zlar, ya’ni predlog, artikl, yordamchi fe’l esa kuchsiz shaklga o‘tadi va unlisi ko‘pincha shva, ya’ni /ə/ bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: I want to go to the shops. Listen: I WANT tə GO tə thə SHOPS. The small words shrink so the big words can keep the beat.
scenes.say_uz: Men do‘konga bormoqchiman. Tinglang: urg‘uli so‘zlar ritmni ushlaydi, kichik so‘zlar esa qisqaradi.

scenes.title: Eng muhim kuchsiz shakllar
board: to /tə/ · of /əv/ → /ə/ · and /ən/ → /n/
can /kən/ · for /fə/ · from /frəm/
was /wəz/ · were /wə/ · have /əv/

examples.t: A cup of tea and a slice of cake.
examples.uz: Bir piyola choy va bir bo‘lak tort.

scenes.say_native: Eng ko‘p uchraydigan kuchsiz shakllarni yodlang. To: /tə/. Of: /əv/, tez nutqda hatto /ə/. And: /ən/ yoki faqat /n/, masalan “fish and chips” “fish ’n’ chips” bo‘ladi. Can: /kən/. Was: /wəz/. Have yordamchi fe’l sifatida /əv/: “could have” “coulda” kabi eshitiladi. Shuning uchun ba’zi inglizlar xatda “could of” deb xato yozadi.
scenes.say: A cup of tea and a slice of cake becomes a cuppa tea 'n' a slice a cake. He could have come sounds like he coulda come.
scenes.say_uz: A cup of tea and a slice of cake tez nutqda deyarli “a cuppa tea ’n’ a slice a cake” bo‘ladi. He could have come esa “he coulda come” kabi eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Bog‘lanish: undosh va unli
board: C + V: turn it off → tur-ni-toff
Linking r (UK): far away → fa-ra-way
Intrusive r (UK): law and order → law-r-and
scenes.say_native: Linking, ya’ni bog‘lanish. So‘z undosh bilan tugab, keyingisi unli bilan boshlansa, undosh keyingi so‘zga o‘tadi: “turn it off” “tur-ni-toff” bo‘lib eshitiladi. Britan nutqida yozuvdagi r odatda talaffuz qilinmaydi, lekin unli oldidan qaytadi: “far away”. Hatto r yozilmagan joyda ham qo‘shilishi mumkin: “law and order”, “the idea of it”. Bu intrusive r deyiladi.
scenes.say: Turn it off. Pick it up. Far away. Law and order. Hear how the words run into each other, with no gaps.
scenes.say_uz: O‘chir. Ko‘tar. Uzoqda. Qonun va tartib. So‘zlar orasida bo‘shliq yo‘q, ular bir-biriga quyilib ketadi.

scenes.title: Elizia: tovush tushib qoladi
board: /t/ /d/ between consonants disappear
next week /neks wiːk/ · last night /lɑːs naɪt/
handbag /ˈhæmbæɡ/ · friendship /ˈfrenʃɪp/
scenes.say_native: Elizia, ya’ni tovushning tushib qolishi. Eng ko‘p t va d ikki undosh orasida yo‘qoladi: “next week” “neks week”, “last night” “las night”, “friendship” esa d siz aytiladi. Bu dangasalik emas, tabiiy tez nutq. O‘zbek tilida ham shunga o‘xshash holat bor: “do‘st bilan” tez aytilganda t ko‘pincha deyarli eshitilmaydi. Demak bu hodisa sizga notanish emas.
scenes.say: Next week. Last night. Handbag. The t and d are written, but in natural speech they've quietly disappeared.
scenes.say_uz: Keyingi hafta. Kecha kechqurun. Sumka. T va d yozilgan, lekin tabiiy nutqda ular jimgina yo‘qolgan.

scenes.title: Assimilyatsiya: tovush o‘zgaradi
board: ten boys → /tem bɔɪz/ · good girl → /ɡʊɡ ɡɜːl/
did you → /ˈdɪdʒu/ · don’t you → /ˈdəʊntʃu/
would you → /ˈwʊdʒu/
scenes.say_native: Assimilyatsiya: bir tovush qo‘shnisiga moslashadi. “Ten boys” da n lab tovushi b oldidan m ga aylanadi. “Good girl” da d g ga yaqinlashadi. Eng muhimi: d yoki t va you birikmasi. “Did you” “didju”, “don’t you” “dontchu”, “would you” “wudju” bo‘ladi. O‘zbek tilida ham “shanba” so‘zi ko‘pincha “shamba” deb aytiladi, bu xuddi shu jarayon.
scenes.say: Did you see it? Would you mind? Don't you think so? Listen for didju, wudju and dontchu.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘rdingmi? Qarshi emasmisiz? Shunday deb o‘ylamaysizmi? Didju, wudju va dontchu ni eshiting.

scenes.title: Norasmiy qisqarishlar
board: going to → gonna · want to → wanna
got to → gotta · don’t know → dunno
let me → lemme · kind of → kinda

examples.t: I'm gonna grab a coffee. Wanna come?

scenes.say_native: Endi norasmiy qisqarishlar. Gonna, wanna, gotta, dunno, lemme, kinda. Ular og‘zaki nutqda juda keng tarqalgan, filmlar va podkastlarda doim eshitasiz. Bitta nozik qoida: “going to” faqat kelasi zamon ma’nosida gonna bo‘ladi. “I’m going to the shop” da joyga borish, shuning uchun gonna demaymiz. Bu shakllarni tanib oling, lekin rasmiy yozuvda ishlatmang.
scenes.say: I'm gonna grab a coffee. Wanna come? I dunno, I've gotta finish this. Lemme check. Pure everyday English.
scenes.say_uz: Kofe olgani boryapman. Kelasanmi? Bilmadim, buni tugatishim kerak. Bir qaray-chi. Sof kundalik ingliz tili.

scenes.title: O‘zbek va rus tili bilan qiyos
board: Uzbek: syllable-timed, vowels stay clear
Russian: unstressed o → a (молоко)
English: unstressed vowels → /ə/
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida bo‘g‘inlar deyarli bir xil uzunlikda va unlilar aniq aytiladi. Shuning uchun biz ingliz tilini ham har bir so‘zni to‘liq aytib gapiramiz va tinglashda ham shuni kutamiz. Rus tilini bilsangiz, sizga yordam bor: “молоко” so‘zi “malako” deb aytilgani kabi, ingliz tilida ham urg‘usiz unlilar kuchsizlanadi. Faqat ingliz tilida ular ko‘pincha shvaga aylanadi.
scenes.say: If you know Russian, you already have a head start. Unstressed vowels weaken there too. English simply goes further.
scenes.say_uz: Rus tilini bilsangiz, sizda allaqachon ustunlik bor. U yerda ham urg‘usiz unlilar kuchsizlanadi. Ingliz tili shunchaki uzoqroq boradi.

scenes.title: Lug‘at shaklini kutish
board: ✗ Waiting to hear /tuː/ in “to”
✓ Expect /tə/ and listen for stressed words
✗ Writing “gonna” in an essay
✓ Recognise it, don’t write it formally
scenes.say_native: Ikki xato. Birinchisi: lug‘atdagi to‘liq shaklni kutish. Agar siz “to” so‘zini /tuː/ deb kutsangiz, uni hech qachon eshitmaysiz va gapni yo‘qotgandek his qilasiz. Kuchsiz shaklni kuting va urg‘uli so‘zlarga quloq tuting. Ikkinchisi: qisqarishlarni yozuvga ko‘chirish. Gonna, wanna esse yoki rasmiy xatda bo‘lmasligi kerak.
scenes.say: Don't wait for the dictionary version of to; you'll be waiting forever. And don't put gonna in your essay.
scenes.say_uz: To ning lug‘at shaklini kutmang, abadiy kutib qolasiz. Va essega gonna yozmang.

scenes.title: Mashq: qisqarishni oching
board: 1 Whaddaya think?
2 I shoulda told her.
3 Didja get it?
4 Gimme a sec.
5 We’re kinda lost.
scenes.say_native: Endi siz. Doskada beshta og‘zaki shakl yozilgan. Har birini to‘liq, yozma inglizchaga aylantiring. Masalan, “wanna” uchun “want to” deysiz. Ikkinchi gapga e’tibor bering: u yerda “of” emas, boshqa so‘z yashiringan. Uchinchi gapda esa yod koalesensiyani eslang. Pauza qiling va yozing.
scenes.say: Turn each spoken form into full written English. Watch number two carefully. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir og‘zaki shaklni to‘liq yozma ingliz tiliga aylantiring. Ikkinchi gapga diqqat qiling. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: qisqarishlar
board: 1 What do you think?
2 I should have told her.
3 Did you get it?
4 Give me a second.
5 We’re kind of lost.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchi: What do you think. Ikkinchi: I should have told her, ya’ni “shoulda” ichida “have” yashiringan, “of” emas. Uchinchi: Did you get it, bu yerda yod koalesensiya, ya’ni d va you birikib “dja” bo‘lgan. To‘rtinchi: Give me a second, “sec” esa “second” ning qisqasi. Beshinchi: We’re kind of lost. Beshtasini topgan bo‘lsangiz, ajoyib.
scenes.say: What do you think? I should have told her. Did you get it? Give me a second. We're kind of lost.
scenes.say_uz: Nima deb o‘ylaysan? Unga aytishim kerak edi. Oldingmi? Bir soniya. Biz biroz adashdik.

scenes.title: Britaniya va Amerika: asosiy farqlar
board: UK (SSBE): car /kɑː/ — no r · US: /kɑːr/ — r
bath: UK /bɑːθ/ · US /bæθ/
lot: UK /lɒt/ · US /lɑːt/

examples.t: Can't you park the car near the bath house?

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi nuqta: asosiy aksentlar. Standart janubiy britan talaffuzi, ya’ni RP yoki SSBE, non-rhotic: unli dan keyingi r aytilmaydi, “car” /kɑː/. Umumiy Amerika talaffuzi rhotic: r har doim eshitiladi. “Bath”, “can’t”, “dance” kabi so‘zlarda Britaniyada uzun /ɑː/, Amerikada /æ/. “Lot”, “hot” da Britaniyada yumaloq /ɒ/, Amerikada ochiq /ɑː/.
scenes.say: Car. Bath. Lot. Listen to the British version, then imagine the American one: a clear r, a flatter a, and a more open o.
scenes.say_uz: Car. Bath. Lot. Britancha variantni tinglang, keyin amerikachasini tasavvur qiling: aniq r, yassiroq a va ochiqroq o.

scenes.title: Flap t va bo‘g‘iz to‘xtashi
board: US flap t: water [ˈwɑːɾɚ] · better · a lot of
UK glottal stop: not now [nɒʔ naʊ] · football
Both: t is not a clear /t/
scenes.say_native: Ikki muhim t hodisasi. Amerika ingliz tilida unlilar orasidagi t yumshoq, tez tovushga aylanadi, u d ga o‘xshab eshitiladi: “water”, “better”, “a lot of”. Britaniyada, ayniqsa kundalik nutqda, t ko‘pincha bo‘g‘iz to‘xtashiga aylanadi: “not now”, “football”. Ikkala holatda ham aniq t yo‘q, shuning uchun “t qayerda?” deb hayron bo‘lmang.
scenes.say: A lot of water. Better butter. In American English the t taps lightly, almost like a d. In casual British speech it often stops in the throat.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘p suv. Yaxshiroq sariyog‘. Amerika ingliz tilida t yengil urilib, deyarli d kabi eshitiladi. Britaniyaning kundalik nutqida esa ko‘pincha bo‘g‘izda to‘xtaydi.

scenes.title: Shotlandiya va Irlandiya
board: Scottish: rhotic r · loch /lɒx/ (= Uzbek x)
Irish: rhotic · th → t/d: three ≈ “tree”
Both: clear r after vowels

examples.t: It's a braw day on the loch.

scenes.say_native: Shotland va Irland aksentlari rhotic, ya’ni r aniq eshitiladi, bu jihatdan ular Amerikaga yaqin. Shotlandiyada “loch” so‘zida o‘zbekcha x tovushi bor, bu sizga qulay. Irlandiyada ko‘p so‘zlovchilar th o‘rniga t yoki d ga yaqin tovush aytadi: “three” “tree” kabi eshitilishi mumkin. Kontekst yordamida buni tez tushunasiz.
scenes.say: In many Scottish and Irish accents the r after a vowel is clearly pronounced. And in Irish English, think and three may sound close to tink and tree.
scenes.say_uz: Ko‘p shotland va irland aksentlarida unlidan keyingi r aniq aytiladi. Irland ingliz tilida esa think va three tink va tree ga yaqin eshitilishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Shimoliy Angliya va Avstraliya
board: Northern England: bus, cup → /ʊ/ (as in put)
bath → short /a/
Australia: non-rhotic · day sounds close to “die”
Rising tone on statements is common
scenes.say_native: Shimoliy Angliyada “bus” va “cup” so‘zlaridagi unli “put” dagi /ʊ/ kabi aytiladi, “bath” esa qisqa a bilan. Avstraliya aksenti Britaniyaga o‘xshab non-rhotic, lekin unlilar boshqacha: “day” so‘zi chet elliklarga “die” ga yaqin eshitiladi. Avstraliyada, va boshqa joylarda ham, oddiy darak gap oxirida ohang ko‘tarilishi mumkin, bu savol degani emas.
scenes.say: Up north, a cup of tea on the bus sounds rather different. And in Australia, a good day can sound a bit like a good die, to outsiders at least.
scenes.say_uz: Shimolda avtobusdagi bir piyola choy ancha boshqacha eshitiladi. Avstraliyada esa good day, hech bo‘lmasa chet elliklarga, good die ga biroz o‘xshab eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Hind ingliz tili va global ingliz
board: Indian English: retroflex t/d, syllable-timed rhythm
Many speakers: v and w sound similar
Uzbek parallel: Toshkent, Xorazm, Farg‘ona shevalari
scenes.say_native: Bugun ingliz tilida ona tili sifatida gaplashadiganlardan ko‘ra, uni ikkinchi til sifatida ishlatadiganlar ko‘proq. Hind ingliz tilida t va d tilning uchi orqaga bukilib aytiladi, ritm esa bo‘g‘inli, o‘zbek tiliga yaqinroq. O‘zbek tilini o‘ylang: toshkentlik, xorazmlik va farg‘onalik bir-birini tushunadi, ammo talaffuz farq qiladi. Ingliz aksentlari ham shunday: hammasi to‘g‘ri, faqat farqli.
scenes.say: There is no single correct accent. A doctor in Mumbai, a farmer in Yorkshire and a lawyer in Texas all speak real English.
scenes.say_uz: Yagona to‘g‘ri aksent yo‘q. Mumbaydagi shifokor, Yorkshirdagi fermer va Texasdagi advokat hammasi haqiqiy ingliz tilida gapiradi.

scenes.title: Can va can’t ni adashtirish
board: ✗ Listening only for the final t
✓ can = weak /kən/, unstressed
✓ can’t = stressed: UK /kɑːnt/ · US /kænt/

examples.t: I can come. / I CAN'T come.

scenes.say_native: Juda xavfli xato: can va can’t ni oxiridagi t bo‘yicha farqlashga urinish. Tez nutqda t deyarli eshitilmaydi. Haqiqiy farq urg‘u va unlida. Ijobiy “can” kuchsiz: /kən/, urg‘u fe’lga tushadi: “I can COME”. Inkor “can’t” urg‘uli: Britaniyada /kɑːnt/, Amerikada /kænt/. Shuning uchun “I CAN’T come” da can’t to‘liq va kuchli eshitiladi.
scenes.say: I can come. I can't come. Don't listen for the t. Listen for the stress: weak can, strong can't.
scenes.say_uz: Kela olaman. Kela olmayman. T ga quloq solmang. Urg‘uga quloq soling: kuchsiz can, kuchli can't.

scenes.title: Mashq: qaysi aksent?
board: 1 r after vowels is silent; bath has a long /ɑː/
2 water sounds like “wadder”; car has a clear r
3 cup rhymes with put; bath has a short a
4 three sounds close to “tree”; clear r
scenes.say_native: Har bir tavsif qaysi aksentga to‘g‘ri keladi? Variantlar: standart britan, umumiy Amerika, shimoliy Angliya va irland. Har bir javob uchun doskadagi bitta belgini dalil sifatida ko‘rsating. Esda tuting, ba’zi belgilar bir nechta aksentda uchraydi, shuning uchun ikkala belgini birga ko‘ring. Pauza qiling.
scenes.say: Match each description with an accent: standard British, General American, Northern English or Irish. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir tavsifni aksent bilan moslang: standart britan, umumiy Amerika, shimoliy Angliya yoki irland. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: aksentlar
board: 1 Standard British (SSBE)
2 General American
3 Northern English
4 Irish
scenes.say_native: Birinchisi standart britan: r aytilmaydi va “bath” da uzun /ɑː/. Ikkinchisi umumiy Amerika: flap t va aniq r. Uchinchisi shimoliy Angliya: “cup” va “put” bir xil unli bilan, “bath” qisqa a bilan. To‘rtinchisi irland: th o‘rniga t ga yaqin tovush va r aniq. Ko‘ryapsizmi, bitta emas, ikkita belgini birga ko‘rish ishonchli javob beradi.
scenes.say: One: standard British. Two: General American. Three: Northern English. Four: Irish. Two features together give you a confident answer.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi: standart britan. Ikkinchi: umumiy Amerika. Uchinchi: shimoliy Angliya. To‘rtinchi: irland. Ikki belgi birgalikda ishonchli javob beradi.

scenes.title: Telegramma usuli
board: Fast speech = stressed words + “noise”
Catch the stressed words → the telegram
TRAIN · DELAYED · HOUR · SIGNAL

examples.t: I'm afraid the train's been delayed by about an hour because of a signal problem.
examples.uz: Afsuski, poyezd signal muammosi tufayli taxminan bir soatga kechikdi.

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi nuqta: tezlikda tushunish. Siz har bir so‘zni eshitishingiz shart emas. Urg‘uli so‘zlar telegramma kabi asosiy ma’noni beradi: “train, delayed, hour, signal”. Qolgan kuchsiz so‘zlar grammatik bog‘lovchi, ularni miya o‘zi tiklaydi. Shuning uchun diqqatingizni urg‘uli so‘zlarga qarating, kichik so‘zlar uchun vahimaga tushmang.
scenes.say: I'm afraid the train's been delayed by about an hour because of a signal problem. Train, delayed, hour, signal. That's the message.
scenes.say_uz: Afsuski, poyezd signal muammosi tufayli taxminan bir soatga kechikdi. Poyezd, kechikdi, soat, signal. Asosiy xabar shu.

scenes.title: Bo‘laklab tinglash va bashorat
board: Listen in chunks, not words
Signposts predict what comes next:
the thing is → a problem · having said that → contrast
to be fair → a defence · long story short → summary
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi usul: so‘zma-so‘z emas, bo‘laklab tinglash va bashorat qilish. So‘zlovchilar nutqida yo‘l ko‘rsatkichlar bor. “The thing is” dan keyin muammo keladi. “Having said that” qarama-qarshi fikrni bildiradi. “To be fair” kimnidir himoya qiladi. “Long story short” xulosa beradi. Bu iboralarni eshitganingizda, keyingi gap nima haqida bo‘lishini oldindan bilasiz va miyangiz tayyor turadi.
scenes.say: The thing is, we're out of budget. Having said that, there might be another option. Signposts tell you what's coming before it arrives.
scenes.say_uz: Gap shundaki, byudjetimiz tugadi. Shunday bo‘lsa-da, boshqa variant bo‘lishi mumkin. Yo‘l ko‘rsatkichlar nima kelishini u kelmasidan oldin aytadi.

scenes.title: Quloqni qanday mashq qildirish kerak
board: 1 Listen at 0.75× with transcript
2 Then 1× without transcript
3 Shadow: repeat half a second behind
4 Then try 1.25×
scenes.say_native: Tezlikka mashq bilan erishiladi. Mana usul: avval audio yoki videoni 0,75 tezlikda matni bilan tinglang. Keyin oddiy tezlikda matnsiz. Keyin shadowing qiling, ya’ni so‘zlovchidan yarim soniya ortda qolib, uning ohangi va ritmini takrorlang. Oxirida 1,25 tezlikda sinab ko‘ring. Kuniga o‘n besh daqiqa bunday mashq bir oyda sezilarli natija beradi.
scenes.say: Slow it down with the transcript, then normal speed without it. Then shadow the speaker. Finally, speed it up and notice how much you still catch.
scenes.say_uz: Matn bilan sekinlashtiring, keyin oddiy tezlikda matnsiz tinglang. Keyin so‘zlovchini soya kabi takrorlang. Oxirida tezlashtiring va hali ham qancha tushunayotganingizni payqang.

scenes.title: Boshda tarjima qilish
board: ✗ Translating each word into Uzbek
✓ Build a picture from the stressed words
✗ Stopping after one missed word
scenes.say_native: Ko‘p o‘quvchilar tinglayotganda har bir so‘zni o‘zbekchaga tarjima qilishga urinadi. Tez nutqda bunga vaqt yo‘q: siz bitta so‘zni tarjima qilguncha, so‘zlovchi uch gapni aytib bo‘ladi. Buning o‘rniga urg‘uli so‘zlardan ichki rasm chizing: kim, nima, qachon. Bitta so‘z tushib qolsa, to‘xtamang. Bu haqda keyingi qismda gaplashamiz.
scenes.say: If you translate every word, you'll always be three sentences behind. Build a picture instead: who, what, when.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir so‘zni tarjima qilsangiz, doim uch gap ortda qolasiz. Uning o‘rniga rasm chizing: kim, nima, qachon.

scenes.title: Mashq: telegrammadan gap tuzing
board: Stressed words only:
1 MEETING · MOVED · THURSDAY · THREE
2 FORGOT · KEYS · CAR
3 WON’T · MAKE · TONIGHT · SORRY
scenes.say_native: Bu yerda faqat urg‘uli so‘zlar berilgan, xuddi tez nutqdan eshitganingizdek. Har bir telegrammadan to‘liq, tabiiy ingliz gapini tiklang. Kuchsiz so‘zlarni, ya’ni artikl, predlog va yordamchi fe’llarni o‘zingiz qo‘shing. Bir nechta to‘g‘ri variant bo‘lishi mumkin, eng tabiiysini tanlang. Pauza qiling.
scenes.say: Here are only the stressed words. Rebuild a natural sentence from each telegram. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Bu yerda faqat urg‘uli so‘zlar. Har bir telegrammadan tabiiy gap tiklang. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: telegrammalar
board: 1 The meeting’s been moved to Thursday at three.
2 I forgot my keys in the car.
3 I won’t make it tonight, sorry.
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javoblar. Birinchi: The meeting’s been moved to Thursday at three. Ikkinchi: I forgot my keys in the car, yoki I left my keys in the car. Uchinchi: I won’t make it tonight, sorry. Bu yerda “make it” iborasi muhim, u “ulgurmoq, kela olmoq” degani. Sizning gapingiz biroz boshqacha bo‘lsa ham, ma’no bir xil bo‘lsa, siz tez nutqni tushungan bo‘lardingiz.
scenes.say: The meeting's been moved to Thursday at three. I forgot my keys in the car. I won't make it tonight, sorry.
scenes.say_uz: Yig‘ilish payshanba soat uchga ko‘chirildi. Kalitlarimni mashinada unutibman. Bugun kecha kela olmayman, kechirasiz.

scenes.title: So‘z tushib qolsa: to‘xtamang
board: Missed a word? Keep listening.
Later context often repairs the gap
Mark it mentally, fill it in later
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi nuqta: eshitmay qolgan so‘z strategiyasi. Eng muhim qoida: to‘xtamang. Bitta so‘z ustida o‘ylab qolsangiz, keyingi uch gapni ham yo‘qotasiz. Bo‘shliqni xayolan belgilab qo‘ying va tinglashda davom eting. Ko‘pincha keyingi gap yo‘qolgan so‘zni tushuntirib beradi yoki takrorlaydi. Imtihonda ham, suhbatda ham bu eng foydali odat.
scenes.say: Missed something? Let it go and keep listening. Speakers repeat, rephrase and explain, and the gap often fills itself.
scenes.say_uz: Nimanidir eshitmadingizmi? Qo‘yib yuboring va tinglashda davom eting. So‘zlovchilar takrorlaydi, qayta ifodalaydi va tushuntiradi, bo‘shliq ko‘pincha o‘z-o‘zidan to‘ladi.

scenes.title: Grammatika va kollokatsiya yordamida tiklash
board: She was … the award. → presented with / given
We need to … a decision. → make / reach
He’s been … since Monday. → off sick / away
scenes.say_native: Bo‘shliqni tiklashda grammatika va kollokatsiya yordam beradi. “She was … the award” gapida bo‘sh joydagi passiv shakl va “award” so‘zi “given” yoki “presented with” bo‘lishini bildiradi. “a decision” oldida deyarli har doim “make” yoki “reach” keladi. “He’s been … since Monday” gapida kontekstga qarab “off sick” yoki “away”. Siz so‘zni aniq eshitmagan bo‘lsangiz ham, ma’noni deyarli to‘g‘ri tiklaysiz.
scenes.say: We need to... something... a decision by Friday. Make, of course. Collocations fill gaps faster than your ears can.
scenes.say_uz: Juma kunigacha qaror... nimadir... kerak. Albatta, qabul qilishimiz. Kollokatsiyalar bo‘shliqni quloqdan tezroq to‘ldiradi.

scenes.title: Raqam va ismlar
board: fifTEEN /fɪfˈtiːn/ vs FIFty /ˈfɪfti/
Stress tells you: -teen at the end, -ty at the start
Names: Could you spell that for me?
scenes.say_native: Raqamlar va ismlar eng xavfli joylar, chunki ularni kontekstdan tiklab bo‘lmaydi. Fifteen va fifty, thirteen va thirty farqi urg‘uda: “-teen” bilan tugaydiganlarda urg‘u oxirida, “-ty” bilan tugaydiganlarda boshida. Lekin sanab aytganda bu urg‘u siljishi mumkin, shuning uchun muhim raqamni har doim tekshiring. Ismlarni esa harflab berishni so‘rang.
scenes.say: It's fifteen pounds, not fifty. Thirteen, thirty. When a number really matters, check it. When a name matters, ask for the spelling.
scenes.say_uz: O‘n besh funt, ellik emas. O‘n uch, o‘ttiz. Raqam haqiqatan muhim bo‘lsa, tekshiring. Ism muhim bo‘lsa, harflab berishni so‘rang.

scenes.title: Aniqlashtirish iboralari
board: Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that.
Did you say fifteen or fifty?
Sorry, you lost me after “budget”.
Could you run that by me again?
scenes.say_native: Suhbatda so‘zni eshitmay qolsangiz, aniq so‘rang. “Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that” umumiy va xushmuomala. Yaxshirog‘i, aynan qaysi qism tushib qolganini ko‘rsatish: “Did you say fifteen or fifty?” yoki “Sorry, you lost me after budget”. “Could you run that by me again?” esa butun tushuntirishni qaytarishni so‘raydi. Aniq savol vaqtni tejaydi va sizni malakali ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Did you say fifteen or fifty? You lost me after budget. Could you run that by me again?
scenes.say_uz: Kechirasiz, yaxshi eshitmadim. O‘n besh dedingizmi yoki ellik? Byudjetdan keyin tushunmay qoldim. Buni yana bir bor tushuntirib bera olasizmi?

scenes.title: Juda keskin so‘rash
board: ✗ What? · Repeat, please.
✓ Sorry, what was that?
✓ Sorry, could you say the last part again?
scenes.say_native: Ko‘p o‘zbek o‘quvchilar so‘ralganda “What?” yoki “Repeat, please” deydi. Grammatik jihatdan xato emas, lekin ingliz qulog‘iga juda keskin, hatto qo‘pol eshitiladi. “Sorry” bilan boshlang va savolni yumshating: “Sorry, what was that?” yoki “Sorry, could you say the last part again?”. Rus tilidagi “Повторите” ning to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri tarjimasidan ham saqlaning.
scenes.say: What? Repeat, please. Too blunt. Try: Sorry, what was that? Or: Sorry, could you say the last part again?
scenes.say_uz: Nima? Takrorlang. Juda keskin. Bunday deng: Kechirasiz, nima dedingiz? Yoki: Kechirasiz, oxirgi qismini yana aytib bera olasizmi?

scenes.title: Mashq: nima deysiz?
board: 1 You missed the price: “It’s ...teen or ...ty pounds”
2 You missed everything after “deadline”
3 You missed the client’s surname
4 The whole explanation was too fast
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta vaziyat. Har birida nimanidir eshitmay qoldingiz. Har bir vaziyat uchun tabiiy, xushmuomala va aniq bitta ibora ayting. Iloji boricha aynan qaysi qism tushib qolganini ko‘rsating. “What?” yoki “Repeat, please” demang. Pauza qiling va ovoz chiqarib ayting.
scenes.say: Four situations. For each, say one polite, precise question. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta vaziyat. Har biri uchun bitta xushmuomala va aniq savol ayting. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: aniqlashtirish
board: 1 Sorry, did you say fifteen or fifty?
2 Sorry, you lost me after “deadline”.
3 Could you spell the surname for me?
4 Could you run that by me again, a bit more slowly?
scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javoblar. Birinchi: “Sorry, did you say fifteen or fifty?”. Ikkinchi: “Sorry, you lost me after deadline”. Uchinchi: “Could you spell the surname for me?”. To‘rtinchi: “Could you run that by me again, a bit more slowly?”. E’tibor bering, har biri “sorry” yoki “could you” bilan yumshatilgan va aniq qismni ko‘rsatadi. Sizning variantingiz ham shunday bo‘lsa, a’lo.
scenes.say: Did you say fifteen or fifty? You lost me after deadline. Could you spell the surname for me? Could you run that by me again, a bit more slowly?
scenes.say_uz: O‘n besh dedingizmi yoki ellik? Muddatdan keyin tushunmay qoldim. Familiyani harflab bera olasizmi? Buni yana bir bor, biroz sekinroq tushuntira olasizmi?

scenes.title: Tinglash 1: ikki britaniyalik do‘st
board: Listen: two friends in London, fast and casual
Focus: plans, times, reduced forms
scenes.say_native: Birinchi tinglash. Londondagi ikki do‘st kechki rejani muhokama qilmoqda. Ular tez va norasmiy gapiradi, kuchsiz shakllar va qisqarishlar ko‘p. Telegramma usulini qo‘llang: urg‘uli so‘zlarni ushlang. Diqqat qiling: ular qayerga boradi, soat nechada va nima uchun reja o‘zgardi?
scenes.say: Tom: You still up for tonight? Amy: Yeah, course. What time d'you reckon? Tom: Well, I was gonna say seven, but Jack's stuck at work, so let's say half eight. Amy: Half eight's fine. Same place? Tom: Nah, the Crown's shut for repairs. We're gonna try that new Thai place by the station. Amy: Oh, I've heard it's good. Should I book? Tom: Already done. Table for four. Amy: Brilliant. See you there, then.
scenes.say_uz: Tom: Bugun kechqurunga hali ham tayyormisan? Emi: Ha, albatta. Soat nechada deb o‘ylaysan? Tom: Yettida demoqchi edim, lekin Jek ishda qolib ketdi, shuning uchun sakkiz yarimda bo‘la qolsin. Emi: Sakkiz yarim ma’qul. O‘sha joydami? Tom: Yo‘q, Kraun ta’mirga yopilgan. Bekat yonidagi yangi Tailand restoranini sinab ko‘ramiz. Emi: Yaxshi deb eshitganman. Joy band qilaymi? Tom: Qilib qo‘ydim. To‘rt kishilik stol. Emi: Zo‘r. Unda o‘sha yerda ko‘rishamiz.

scenes.title: Savollar: 1-tinglash
board: 1 What time will they meet, and why?
2 Why aren’t they going to the Crown?
3 How many people is the table for?
4 Write the full form of: d’you reckon · gonna · Nah
scenes.say_native: Dialog bo‘yicha to‘rtta savol. Ular soat nechada uchrashadi va nima uchun vaqt o‘zgardi? Nega Crown ga bormaydi? Stol necha kishiga band qilingan? Va oxirgi savol: doskadagi uchta og‘zaki shaklni to‘liq yozma shaklga aylantiring. Pauza qiling va javob yozing.
scenes.say: Four questions. What time, and why? Why not the Crown? A table for how many? And write the full forms. Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savol. Soat nechada va nima uchun? Nega Crown emas? Necha kishilik stol? Va to‘liq shakllarni yozing. Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: 1-tinglash
board: 1 Half past eight, because Jack is stuck at work
2 It’s closed for repairs
3 Four
4 do you reckon · going to · No
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: sakkiz yarimda, ya’ni half past eight, chunki Jek ishda qolib ketgan. E’tibor bering, britancha “half eight” sakkiz yarim degani, yetti yarim emas. Ikkinchi: Crown ta’mir uchun yopilgan. Uchinchi: to‘rt kishilik stol. To‘rtinchi: “do you reckon”, ya’ni “nima deb o‘ylaysan”, “going to” va “No”. Half eight ko‘pchilik uchun eng katta tuzoq edi.
scenes.say: Half past eight, because Jack's stuck at work. The Crown is closed for repairs. A table for four. Do you reckon, going to, and no.
scenes.say_uz: Sakkiz yarim, chunki Jek ishda qolib ketgan. Kraun ta’mirga yopilgan. To‘rt kishilik stol. Do you reckon, going to va no.

scenes.title: Tinglash 2: amerikalik hamkasb bilan qo‘ng‘iroq
board: Listen: a phone call with an American colleague
Focus: numbers, the clarification, the deadline
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi tinglash. Dilnoza amerikalik hamkasbi Mark bilan telefonda gaplashmoqda. Mark tez gapiradi va Amerika talaffuzida flap t ko‘p. Dilnoza bir joyni eshitmay qoladi va aniqlashtiradi. Diqqat qiling: qaysi raqam muhim, Dilnoza qanday ibora ishlatdi va muddat qachon?
scenes.say: Mark: So I talked to the client, and they wanna push the launch back. We're looking at, like, the thirteenth now. Dilnoza: Sorry, did you say the thirteenth or the thirtieth? Mark: Thirteenth. One-three. And they need the updated budget a week before that, so, uh, the sixth. Dilnoza: Got it. And the budget, is that the version we sent on Monday? Mark: Pretty much, but they wanna cut the marketing a little. Dilnoza: OK, I'll get that over to you by Friday.
scenes.say_uz: Mark: Mijoz bilan gaplashdim, ular ishga tushirishni orqaga surmoqchi. Endi, taxminan, o‘n uchinchi sana ko‘zda tutilyapti. Dilnoza: Kechirasiz, o‘n uchinchi dedingizmi yoki o‘ttizinchi? Mark: O‘n uchinchi. Bir-uch. Va ularga yangilangan byudjet bir hafta oldin kerak, ya’ni oltinchi. Dilnoza: Tushundim. Byudjet dushanba kuni yuborgan versiyamizmi? Mark: Deyarli, lekin ular marketingni biroz qisqartirmoqchi. Dilnoza: Yaxshi, juma kunigacha sizga yuboraman.

scenes.title: Savollar: 2-tinglash
board: 1 What is the new launch date?
2 Which phrase did Dilnoza use to check?
3 When does the client need the budget?
4 What change does the client want?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol. Yangi ishga tushirish sanasi qachon? Dilnoza qaysi ibora bilan tekshirdi? Mijozga byudjet qachon kerak? Va mijoz byudjetda qanday o‘zgarish xohlaydi? Raqamlarga alohida e’tibor bering, ular bu dialogdagi eng muhim ma’lumot. Pauza qiling.
scenes.say: What's the new launch date? How did Dilnoza check? When is the budget due? What change does the client want? Pause now.
scenes.say_uz: Yangi sana qachon? Dilnoza qanday tekshirdi? Byudjet qachon kerak? Mijoz qanday o‘zgarish xohlaydi? Hozir pauza qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: 2-tinglash
board: 1 The thirteenth (one-three)
2 Did you say the thirteenth or the thirtieth?
3 By the sixth, a week before launch
4 A small cut to marketing
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: o‘n uchinchi sana, Mark “one-three” deb ham tasdiqladi. Ikkinchi: “Did you say the thirteenth or the thirtieth?”, ikki variantni berib so‘rash juda samarali. Uchinchi: oltinchi sanagacha, ishga tushirishdan bir hafta oldin. To‘rtinchi: marketing xarajatlarini biroz qisqartirish. “Wanna”, “like” va “pretty much” kabi so‘zlar sizni chalg‘itmadimi?
scenes.say: The thirteenth. Did you say the thirteenth or the thirtieth? By the sixth. And a small cut to marketing.
scenes.say_uz: O‘n uchinchi. O‘n uchinchi dedingizmi yoki o‘ttizinchi? Oltinchigacha. Va marketingni biroz qisqartirish.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: shadowing
board: Shadow this line 3 times:
I was gonna call you, but I didn’t get a chance.
Then say it slowly, then at full speed
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy vazifa: shadowing. Gapni tinglang va uch marta, so‘zlovchidan yarim soniya ortda qolib takrorlang. Kuchsiz shakllarga e’tibor bering: “gonna”, “but I” bog‘lanishi, “didn’t get a” da t lar yumshaydi. Avval sekin, keyin to‘liq tezlikda ayting. Agar imkon bo‘lsa, o‘zingizni yozib oling va asl nusxa bilan solishtiring.
scenes.say: I was gonna call you, but I didn't get a chance. Shadow it three times, slowly at first, then at full speed.
scenes.say_uz: Senga qo‘ng‘iroq qilmoqchi edim, lekin imkon bo‘lmadi. Uch marta takrorlang, avval sekin, keyin to‘liq tezlikda.

scenes.title: Namuna: nima eshitildi?
board: ɪ wəz ˈɡʌnə ˈkɔːl jə
bə taɪ ˈdɪdn ˈɡet ə ˈtʃɑːns
Stressed: GONNA · CALL · DIDN’T · GET · CHANCE
scenes.say_native: Namunani tahlil qilamiz. “Was” kuchsiz /wəz/, “you” ko‘pincha /jə/ bo‘ladi. “But I” bog‘lanib, t keyingi so‘zga o‘tadi. “Didn’t” dagi t deyarli yo‘qoladi. Urg‘u esa gonna, call, didn’t, get va chance so‘zlarida. Agar siz ham shu beshta urg‘uli so‘zni aniq aytib, qolganini yengil o‘tkazgan bo‘lsangiz, tabiiy ritmni ushlagansiz.
scenes.say: I was GONNA CALL you, but I DIDN'T GET a CHANCE. Five strong beats, everything else light and quick.
scenes.say_uz: Senga qo‘ng‘iroq qilmoqchi edim, lekin imkon bo‘lmadi. Beshta kuchli zarb, qolgan hammasi yengil va tez.

scenes.title: Darsning xulosasi
board: Connected speech: weak forms, linking, elision, assimilation
Accents: rhotic r, bath, flap t, glottal stop
Speed: stressed words + signposts
Missed words: keep going, then check politely
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Birinchi: bog‘langan nutq, ya’ni kuchsiz shakllar, bog‘lanish, elizia va assimilyatsiya. Ikkinchi: asosiy aksentlar, r aytilishi, bath unlisi, flap t va bo‘g‘iz to‘xtashi bo‘yicha farqlanadi. Uchinchi: tezlikda urg‘uli so‘zlar va yo‘l ko‘rsatkichlarga tayaning, tarjima qilmang. To‘rtinchi: so‘z tushib qolsa, tinglashda davom eting, kerak bo‘lsa xushmuomala va aniq so‘rang.
scenes.say: Weak forms and linking, accent features, stressed words and signposts, and a calm strategy for missed words. That's your toolkit.
scenes.say_uz: Kuchsiz shakllar va bog‘lanish, aksent belgilari, urg‘uli so‘zlar va yo‘l ko‘rsatkichlar, hamda eshitilmagan so‘zlar uchun xotirjam strategiya. Mana sizning vositalaringiz.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: Transcribe 30 seconds of fast native speech
Success: every word written, gaps marked
Check with subtitles · find 5 connected-speech features
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: podkast, intervyu yoki filmdan o‘ttiz soniyalik tez nutq parchasini tanlang va uni so‘zma-so‘z yozib chiqing. Mezon: har bir so‘zni yozishga harakat qiling, eshitilmagan joylarni belgilang, keyin subtitr bilan tekshiring va kamida beshta bog‘langan nutq hodisasini toping va nomlang. Keyingi darsda ishontirish va muzokara olib borishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Your homework: transcribe thirty seconds of fast speech, check it against subtitles, and label five connected-speech features. Next time: persuasion and negotiation.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifangiz: o‘ttiz soniyalik tez nutqni yozib chiqing, subtitr bilan tekshiring va beshta bog‘langan nutq hodisasini belgilang. Keyingi dars: ishontirish va muzokara.

homework_uz: Podkast, intervyu yoki filmdan 30 soniyalik tez ingliz nutqini tanlang va uni so‘zma-so‘z yozib chiqing. Mezon: har bir so‘zni yozishga harakat qiling, eshitilmagan joylarni belgilang, keyin subtitr bilan tekshirib, to‘g‘ri yozilgan so‘zlar foizini hisoblang va kamida beshta bog‘langan nutq hodisasini (kuchsiz shakl, bog‘lanish, elizia, assimilyatsiya, qisqarish) topib nomlang.

quiz.q: In fast speech, “I should have known” usually sounds like:
quiz.why_uz: Have kuchsiz /əv/ ga, tez nutqda /ə/ ga aylanadi: shoulda. Yozuvda esa should have.

quiz.q: Which is the full form of “Whaddaya want?”
quiz.why_uz: Whaddaya = what do you. Do va you kuchsizlanib birikadi.

quiz.q: In standard British English, the r in “car park” is:
quiz.why_uz: Standart britan talaffuzi non-rhotic: undosh oldidan va so‘z oxirida r aytilmaydi.

quiz.q: How can you best tell “I can go” from “I can't go”?
options: can is weak /kən/; can't is stressed
quiz.why_uz: T ko‘pincha eshitilmaydi; farq urg‘u va unlida.

quiz.q: In General American, “water” often sounds like:
quiz.why_uz: Amerika ingliz tilida unlilar orasidagi t flap tovushga aylanadi va d ga o‘xshaydi.

quiz.q: What does “half eight” mean in British English?
quiz.why_uz: Britancha half eight = half past eight, ya’ni 8:30.

quiz.q: You missed a price. What is the best question?
options: Sorry, did you say fifteen or fifty?
quiz.why_uz: Sorry bilan yumshatilgan va aniq qismni ko‘rsatadigan savol eng yaxshisi.

quiz.q: “Next week” in natural speech is often pronounced:
quiz.why_uz: Elizia: ikki undosh orasidagi t tushib qoladi.

quiz.q: A speaker says “Having said that...”. What comes next?
quiz.why_uz: Having said that qarama-qarshi fikrni oldindan bildiradi.

quiz.q: In fast speech, which words carry the main message?
quiz.why_uz: Urg‘uli mazmunli so‘zlar telegramma kabi asosiy ma’noni beradi.
